Latvia vs Armenia Live Stream: Kickoff Time, How to Watch & Match Preview

Match Overview

Latvia host Armenia in the final round of UEFA Nations League C Group 2 on 15 November 2026. Kickoff is scheduled for 14:00 UTC. The venue has not been officially confirmed at the time of writing. Latvia enter the fixture bottom of the group with one point from five matches, while Armenia sit third on five points. Both teams have already played each other twice in the current campaign, with Armenia winning both encounters.

This match concludes the group stage. Montenegro have already secured promotion with 13 points, while Cyprus are assured of second place. Armenia cannot overtake Cyprus but could finish third ahead of Latvia, who are already guaranteed last place and a relegation play-off. The result will determine whether Armenia avoid the bottom spot outright.

Why This Match Matters

Latvia are rooted to the bottom of Group 2 with one point from five matches (0 wins, 1 draw, 4 losses). They have scored three goals and conceded eight. A win would lift them to four points but would not change their final position, as they trail Armenia by four points with only this match remaining. Latvia are already destined for the League C/D relegation play-offs.

Armenia occupy third place with five points (1 win, 2 draws, 2 losses), five goals scored and six conceded. They are four points clear of Latvia and three points behind second-placed Cyprus. A draw or win would confirm third place and safety from the relegation play-off. A defeat would still leave them third on goal difference unless Latvia overturn a five-goal swing, which is virtually impossible. For Armenia, the match offers a chance to finish the campaign on a positive note and avoid the play-off bracket entirely.

Cyprus vs Montenegro Live Stream: Kickoff Time, How to Watch & Match Preview

Match Overview

Cyprus face Montenegro in a UEFA Nations League League C Group 2 fixture scheduled for 15 November 2026 with a 14:00 GMT kickoff. The match will be played at Cyprus's home venue, though the specific stadium has not been confirmed at the time of writing. This is the sixth and final matchday of the group stage, with both teams' positions already carrying significant implications for promotion and playoff contention.

Montenegro arrive as group leaders with 13 points from five matches, holding a five-point advantage over second-placed Cyprus who have eight points. Montenegro have secured at least a promotion playoff spot, while Cyprus are competing with Armenia for the second playoff position. The reverse fixture in Montenegro ended in a 4-0 victory for the visitors, making this a crucial opportunity for Cyprus to overturn the goal difference deficit in the head-to-head tiebreaker.

Why This Match Matters

Montenegro sit top of Group 2 with 13 points (W4 D1 L0) and have already guaranteed at least a promotion playoff place. A draw or win would secure top spot and direct promotion to League B. Cyprus are second with eight points (W2 D2 L1) and need a victory to keep alive their hopes of overtaking Montenegro, though the five-point gap makes direct promotion unlikely. A win for Cyprus would move them to 11 points and strengthen their grip on the playoff position ahead of Armenia on five points.

The head-to-head record is critical: Montenegro won the reverse fixture 4-0, giving them a superior goal difference in the direct comparison. Cyprus would need to win by at least five goals to overturn that deficit, making the playoff spot the more realistic target. For Montenegro, avoiding defeat would confirm them as group winners and secure automatic promotion.

Cyprus

In the current Nations League campaign, Cyprus have played five matches: two wins, two draws, and one loss. They have scored six goals and conceded four, averaging 1.20 goals per game and conceding 0.80 per game. Their form sequence reads DWWDL, with the sole defeat coming in the 4-0 loss away to Montenegro. They are unbeaten in their other four fixtures, including draws against Armenia and Latvia.

Montenegro

Montenegro have played five matches: four wins, one draw, and zero losses. They have scored nine goals and conceded five, averaging 1.80 goals per game and conceding 1.00 per game. Their form sequence is WDWWW, with the only dropped points coming in a draw against Armenia. They have won their last three matches consecutively, including the 4-0 victory over Cyprus and wins against Latvia and Armenia.

Spain vs England Live Stream: Kickoff Time, How to Watch & Match Preview

Match Overview

Spain and England meet in UEFA Nations League A Group 3 on 15 November 2026 with kickoff scheduled for 19:45 GMT. The fixture takes place at a venue yet to be confirmed by the competition organisers. Spain currently lead the group with maximum points from five matches, while England sit second, three points behind. This match represents a significant step in determining the group winner and automatic qualification for the Nations League finals.

Spain have won all five group games so far, scoring 14 goals and conceding five. England have four wins and one defeat, with 16 goals scored and four conceded. Both teams have already secured their place in the top two of the group, but the winner of this encounter will take a decisive advantage in the race for first place.

Why This Match Matters

Spain top Group 3 with 15 points from five matches (W5 D0 L0), holding a three-point lead over England who have 12 points (W4 D0 L1). A win for Spain would extend their lead to six points with only one match remaining, effectively securing first place and a spot in the Nations League finals. England need a victory to close the gap to three points and keep their fate in their own hands heading into the final matchday.

Both teams have already guaranteed a top-two finish, avoiding relegation to League B. However, only the group winner advances to the knockout finals tournament. The head-to-head result could also serve as a tiebreaker if the teams finish level on points. Spain's superior goal difference (+9 vs +12 for England) adds another layer to the calculation.

Current Season Statistics

Spain

In the current Nations League campaign, Spain have played five matches, winning all five, drawing none and losing none. They have scored 14 goals (2.8 per game) and conceded five (1.0 per game). Their goal difference stands at +9. Spain are on a five-match winning streak in the competition.

England

England have played five matches in the current Nations League campaign, winning four and losing one. They have scored 16 goals (3.2 per game) and conceded four (0.8 per game). Their goal difference is +12. England's only defeat came in their most recent match, ending a four-match winning run.

Players to Watch

Spain

Rodri (Midfielder) – The Manchester City pivot controls tempo, breaks opposition attacks and initiates Spain's possession game. His presence allows the creative midfielders to operate higher up the pitch.

Lamine Yamal (Forward) – The teenage winger provides width, dribbling and goal threat. His one-on-one ability can unlock compact defences and create space for overlapping full-backs.

England

Bukayo Saka (Forward) – The Arsenal winger delivers creativity, direct running and end product. His ability to beat defenders on either foot makes him difficult to contain in wide areas.

Harry Kane (Forward) – England's captain and all-time leading scorer remains the focal point of attack. His hold-up play, passing range and finishing make him a constant danger in and around the box.

Spain enter as group leaders with a perfect record, home advantage (venue pending confirmation) and a psychological edge after beating England in the Euro 2024 final. Their possession-based system under Luis de la Fuente has yielded 14 goals in five matches. England possess greater attacking firepower statistically (16 goals) but suffered a recent defeat that ended their winning run. The head-to-head record over the last five meetings favours Spain (W3 D1 L1).

Considering current form, tactical matchups and the stakes, Spain are slight favourites. England's attacking talent keeps them dangerous on the counter-attack and from set pieces. A tight, competitive match is expected with both teams likely to score.

The venue has not been officially confirmed for this fixture. Croatia enter the match in third place with three points from five matches, while Czech Republic sit bottom of the group without a point. Both teams have already been relegated to League B for the next edition, but pride and FIFA ranking points remain at stake.

Joško Gvardiol (Defender) – The left-sided centre-back provides defensive solidity and attacking overlaps. His duels with Czech wingers will shape the flank battles.

Tomáš Souček (Midfielder) – The West Ham captain brings aerial presence, late runs into the box, and defensive screening. He will be pivotal in disrupting Croatia’s midfield rhythm.

Václav Černý (Winger) – The Rangers winger provides pace and directness on the counter. His one-on-one ability could exploit spaces left by Croatia’s advancing full-backs.

Croatia’s superior squad depth, home advantage, and recent 5–1 win over Czech Republic in June 2025 point to a likely victory. Czech Republic have lost all five Nations League matches, scoring only twice. Croatia’s attack has shown signs of life with five goals, and Kramarić’s form suggests they can breach a fragile Czech defence. However, the dead-rubber context may reduce intensity, and Czech Republic’s pride could produce a tighter contest than the scoreline suggests.
